issues.title: Invalid seminorm substitution in the stability estimate

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $C_S$ and $C_S^{\prime}$ denote the constants of the Sobolev embeddings $H^1(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^6(\Omega)$ and $H^1(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^3(\Omega)$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Interpolation gives a factor involving \(\|e\|_{H^1}^{1/2}\), not \(|e|_{H^1}^{1/2}\). The stability theorem allows an arbitrary perturbed solution and residual, so the error need not have zero mean. For near-constant errors \(e=M+\varepsilon\phi\), the claimed transition scales like \(\varepsilon M^2\) on the left but \(\varepsilon^{3/2}M^{3/2}\) on the right and fails for small \(\varepsilon\). Consequently, the displayed energy estimate does not prove the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Neither stability framework, their existence corollaries, nor the two corresponding parts of the main estimator are established with the printed nonlinear estimate and constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the nonlinear estimate with x = ||e||_{L2} and g = |e|_{H1}: the valid interpolation gives II <= C(g x^2 + g^{3/2}x^{3/2}), and Young's inequality gives II <= epsilon g^2 + C_epsilon(x^4+x^6). Choose epsilon within the existing coercivity budget and use x^4 <= x^2+x^6. The resulting energy inequality has the original Gronwall form after enlarging the linear coefficient and B. Propagate those constants through stab_thm, stab_cont, their existence corollaries, and both parts of main_thm, retaining the stated L-infinity-in-time L2 and L2-in-time H1 bounds.
issues.why_classification: The seminorm substitution is an invalid inference and therefore not a typo. Nevertheless, a routine interpolation/Young split restores the same stability architecture and every affected conclusion, with only changed constants and no new lemma, model restriction, rate loss, or loss of H1 control.

issues.title: Undefined point-sampling initialization for L2 data

failure_location.quote: We start by defining $\rho_h^0 \in R_h$ by $\rho_h^0|_K := \rho_0(x_K)$, for all $K \in\mathcal{T}_h$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which we equip with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions and an initial condition $\rho_0 \in L^2$,

issues.failure_explanation: Changing an L2 representative at the finitely many circumcenters leaves the input unchanged in L2 but can change every sampled value. Hence the old initialization is not a well-defined input-output operation on the stated data class.
issues.overall_effect: The FV-FE algorithm cannot be initialized canonically for all allowed initial data, although the later abstract estimates remain applicable to any separately supplied discrete sequence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every use of the point samples by the cell-average initialization rho_h^0|_K = |K|^{-1} integral_K rho_0, equivalently rho_h^0 = Pi_0 rho_0, and update the later reconstruction text that recalls the initialization. This defines the algorithm on L2 equivalence classes while preserving mass, nonnegativity for nonnegative data, and the remainder of the FV-FE procedure.
issues.why_classification: Point evaluation on L2 data is a genuine construction defect rather than a transcription error, but the cell-average projection is a standard, local, source-supported replacement that preserves the input class and algorithmic guarantees without further analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs a certified computable upper bound for \(\|\nabla\tilde c\|_{L^\infty}\). The old remark supplies only the scalar condition \(q\cdot n=0\) for the vector equation \((I-\Delta)q=\nabla\bar\rho\), without tangential or natural boundary conditions, a weak space, or boundary residuals. On the admissible square, for example, \(q=(\sin(\pi x)\cosh(\sqrt{1+\pi^2}\,y),0)\) is a nonzero solution of the homogeneous vector equation satisfying \(q\cdot n=0\). Thus the stated data do not select the actual gradient, and the FE quantity used by main_thm is not certified.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract stability estimates remain meaningful if the exact gradient norm is known, but the old main theorem's claimed fully computable coefficients and resulting existence certificate are not established on its bounded Neumann domains.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the underdetermined vector problem by a well-posed bounded-domain certificate. On each flat boundary face, formulate the problem in V = {v in H1(Omega)^d : v dot n = 0}, with q dot n imposed essentially and the tangential part of (grad q)n imposed naturally; then q = grad tilde c is the unique variational solution. Use a conforming subspace of V, include the corresponding boundary tangential-flux residuals as well as interior jumps, and establish the maximum-norm reliability bound before using it in a(t), E, and E_n. This retains the bounded polygonal Neumann and mixed-boundary setting and the fully computable main estimator.
issues.why_classification: No symbol-level edit makes the old FE quantity certify the actual gradient. Preserving the stated bounded-domain coefficient requires a new well-posed boundary formulation and a contained but nontrivial maximum-norm reliability argument with boundary residuals. That work is localized and preserves the theorem's model class and guarantee, so it is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Existence certification outside the supplied domain hypotheses

failure_location.quote: Let $d \in \left\{2,3\right\}$ and $\Omega \subset \R^d$ be bounded, polygonal and such that (\ref{ell_reg}) holds.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain in $\R^d$, $d \in \{2,3\}$, with sufficiently smooth boundary.
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain in $\R^d$, $d \in \{2,3\}$, with sufficiently smooth boundary.
and, in particular, $(\rho, c)$ is a weak solution up to time $T$.

issues.failure_explanation: main_thm claims its existence consequence for every bounded polygonal domain satisfying ell_reg. The old paper actually supplies weakexistence and apostverif only for bounded domains with sufficiently smooth boundary. No result extends those inputs to the polygonal domains used by the numerical scheme, so the conditional residual and stability estimates do not support the advertised existence conclusion on the theorem's stated domain class.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional error estimates may still apply once a weak solution is given, but the central a posteriori existence conclusion is unsupported for the old bounded polygonal and mixed-boundary setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply local well-posedness and continuation for the polygonal and claimed mixed-boundary class used by main_thm, rather than invoking the smooth-boundary theorem. A contained Galerkin argument under ell_reg uses ||grad c||_{L6} <= C||rho||_{L2} and H1-to-L6 interpolation to obtain d||rho||_{L2}^2/dt + c||grad rho||_{L2}^2 <= C(||rho||_{L2}^4+||rho||_{L2}^6). This yields a lifespan depending only on the L2 norm and an L2 continuation criterion. State that result for the maximal solution and use it in apostverif and the existence clause of main_thm.
issues.why_classification: The mismatch cannot be cured by merely adding smoothness, since that would remove the polygonal numerical regime. Establishing the needed polygonal-domain local theory and continuation criterion is substantial new PDE work, but it is a self-contained prerequisite that leaves the residual analysis, stability architecture, domain class, and existence guarantee intact; hence the issue is moderate, not serious.

issues.title: Circular use of the full existence interval

failure_location.quote: Let $(\rho,c)$ be a weak solution of the Keller-Segel system (\ref{KS1}), (\ref{KS2}), (\ref{KScond})

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose $(\rho,c)$ is a weak solution of the Keller-Segel system (\ref{KS1}), (\ref{KS2}), (\ref{KScond})
and, in particular, $(\rho, c)$ is a weak solution up to time $T$.

issues.failure_explanation: To serve as an existence proof, the old argument must work before it is known that T<T_max. Instead, main_thm assumes a weak solution and applies stab_thm or stab_cont on [0,T], where those results also assume that solution exists. On a literal reading the existence clause is merely tautological; on the intended certification reading the stability input is unestablished and rho may be evaluated beyond its known maximal interval.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof establishes only an error estimate conditional on prior existence through T, not the advertised numerical certification that the solution extends to T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Quantify the maximal weak solution only on [0,T_max), state the estimator initially on [0,min{T,T_max}), and apply each stability estimate on every shorter interval [0,s] with s < min{T,T_max}. The full-T computable condition dominates its restriction to such intervals, so the bounds are uniform as s approaches min{T,T_max}. Then invoke apostverif to conclude T < T_max.
issues.why_classification: The printed proof is circular, so this is not a typo. However, the old source already contains precisely the required maximal-interval proposition; a routine truncation and continuation argument removes the circularity while preserving the estimator, condition, rate, and existence conclusion.

issues.title: Undefined comparison function in the second estimator

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $(\tilde{\rho},\tilde{c})$ be the reconstruction of our numerical approximation defined in \autoref{Morley}.

issues.failure_explanation: The symbol \(\bar\rho\) is not quantified or defined in main_thm. The theorem's input is \((\tilde\rho,\tilde c)\), and its proof says that this reconstruction is substituted into stab_cont, where \(\bar\rho\) is only the generic perturbed-solution notation. Thus the printed H1 comparison is undefined as written.
issues.overall_effect: Only the H1 component of the second displayed estimator is malformed; the intended comparison and the rest of the theorem are unambiguous from the immediate context.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace bar rho by tilde rho in the H1-seminorm integrand of part ii of main_thm.
issues.why_classification: Main_thm defines only the reconstruction tilde rho, its L2 term already compares rho with tilde rho, and the proof explicitly substitutes that reconstruction into stab_cont. Thus the old source uniquely forces this one-symbol correction, with no mathematical inference or guarantee requiring repair.
